summary: Dashboard annotation layer flickers and drops annotations when applying ad-hoc time shift
description:
Issue summary:
Users report that when they apply an ad-hoc time shift (e.g., shifting the dashboard to -7d) the annotation overlay begins to flicker and several annotations disappear entirely from the view. Behavior is intermittent but reproducible for large time ranges and when the dashboard contains more than ~400 annotations.

Impact:
- Customer GlacierDocs (enterprise) is unable to rely on annotations for post-deployment incident reviews; important markers dropped from charts.
- Affects any org-level dashboard with annotations + ad-hoc time shift; visibility regression for historical analysis.

Environment:
- Console web app (React) v4.8.1 served from prod in us-east region.
- Annotations backed by annotations-service v1.9 (Postgres), served through console API gateway.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login as a user with access to org dashboard that has >400 annotations in the last 90 days.
2) Open dashboard, confirm annotations visible at baseline (no time shift).
3) Open time selector and apply an ad-hoc shift (e.g., Last 30 days with "Shift by" -7d or use the time-shift quick selector).
4) Observe annotation layer flicker; some annotations disappear instantly and do not return when toggling layer visibility.
5) Refresh the dashboard -> sometimes annotations return; applying different shifts causes unpredictable losses.

Observed behavior:
- Flicker of the annotation layer (visual redraw) followed by removal of up to 30-40% of annotations for the selected range.
- Trace links from annotations occasionally break (link -> 404) after the shift.
- No 500s from API, but frontend console shows 'Range mismatch for annotation cache' warnings.

Expected behavior:
- Time shift should re-query annotations for the shifted window and render a stable annotation layer with all markers that fall in the shifted period.

Logs / artifacts attached:
- Console network timeline HAR (redacted) - link in comments.
- Screenshot: flicker and missing markers.
- Frontend console warnings: "annotation-cache: mismatch between server range and client range, invalidating partial cache" (repeated).
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Support):
- Reproduced with GlacierDocs test org. Problem more likely when annotation count > ~400 and when time-shift window size increases tokenized query length to annotations-service.
- Client-side code path: time-shift triggers a new annotation query with range calculation; client attempts to merge incremental annotation pages into existing render layer. Merge logic likely drops annotations that fall outside a previously cached bucket due to inconsistent bucket boundary calculation.

Eng update (Lucas Rivera):
- Checked annotations-service logs for query patterns around 2026-03-10T15:xx. No 5xxs. Query payloads show overlapping but non-identical range parameters between client and gateway (off-by-one in millis conversion). Suspect rounding/UTC conversion bug in client-shift calculation.
- Found related flaky test in PR history that touched range normalization for ad-hoc shifts (see related_github_prs).

SRE note:
- No infra capacity issues. Memory and p99 latency for annotations-service normal. Not a DB timeout.

Hypothesis:
- Client calculates shifted range using timezone-naive timestamps, resulting in queries for ranges that straddle bucket boundaries. Client-side merge code then discards items that don't match exact bucket IDs. The net effect: flicker as layer re-renders and some items dropped permanently until full refresh.
